subtype: Approach: relapse after a festival or exam week and restarting [Revision]
passage:
Dear Shreya,

Thanks for not laughing when I told you about last week. My cousin's wedding meant four nights of bed at three and up at noon, and by Sunday my routine was gone. I sat there feeling as if I'd ruined a whole month of work. Then I remembered what you said: one slip is not a verdict. So on Monday I did only one thing: alarm at seven, curtains open, breakfast. No punishment, no marathon revision. On Tuesday I was tired. By Wednesday I was nearly back, and bedtime came on its own. I keep the wake time fixed and treat the rest as adjustable. Want to walk before school on Thursday?

Harsha

qa.q: How many nights did the wedding shift Harsha's sleep?
qa.a: The wedding meant four nights of bed at three and up at noon.

qa.q: How did Harsha feel on Sunday, and what changed?
qa.a: Harsha felt as if a month of work was ruined, but remembering that one slip is not a verdict made it possible to restart.

qa.q: What else could Harsha do to protect the routine before the next big event, and why?
qa.a: Harsha could keep the wake time as close as possible during the event and plan an easy morning the day after, because a quick restart is easier when the anchor is kept.

qa.q: How might Shreya feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Shreya probably feels glad and useful, since the earlier advice helped Harsha to restart. 🙂

grounding: After a week of late nights around a wedding, the student does not give up but returns to the fixed wake time the next morning, treating the slip as normal rather than proof of failure.
